data.title: Kojic acid + Arbutin + Glycolic acid cream
data.summary: VIII Pigmentary / depigmenting · Non-hydroquinone combination depigmenting cream (cosmeceutical)
data.body:
_Topicals · VIII Pigmentary / depigmenting_

**Class:** Non-hydroquinone combination depigmenting cream (cosmeceutical)

## Mechanism of action
- Kojic acid (fungal metabolite, 1–4%): chelates copper at the tyrosinase active site → inhibits tyrosinase; antioxidant
- Arbutin (glycosylated hydroquinone from bearberry, 1–3%): competitive tyrosinase inhibitor with less melanocytotoxicity than hydroquinone
- Glycolic acid: exfoliates pigmented keratinocytes and enhances penetration

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Melasma (maintenance or hydroquinone-intolerant patients), PIH, mild lentigines
- Maintenance after triple combination cream

## Dose & formulations
- Once daily at night (or twice daily) with daytime sunscreen; results over 8–12 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Irritation, contact dermatitis (kojic acid is a sensitiser)
- Photosensitivity (glycolic acid)
- Kojic acid is unstable — oxidises in air and light

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity; inflamed skin

## Pregnancy & lactation
Limited data; generally considered low risk (arbutin releases small amounts of hydroquinone — use caution).

## Viva points
- Kojic acid chelates copper of tyrosinase
- Arbutin = natural hydroquinone glycoside
- Useful hydroquinone-free maintenance

_Sources: Khopkar ch.26 and ch.29 (Cosmeceuticals); Wolverton 4e ch.57. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
